newsitem.title: USA: Westcoast says B.C. gas plant briefly shut.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast says B.C. gas plant briefly shut.

text.p: Westcoast Energy said Tuesday its McMahon natural gas plant in British Columbia likely would return to service later today after shutting down this morning for unscheduled repairs.
"We'll be back up and running around four (1600 MST/1800) or so this afternoon. The plant was shut at 8 a.m. (0800 MST/1000 EST)," company spokesman Irv Koop said.
About 200 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas was cut as a result of a problem in the control system at the plant, he said.
Total capacity at the plant is about 700 mmcfd.
Despite the brief outage, spot prices at Sumas, Wash., for Wednesday delivery were fairly steady in a range of $1.05-1.10 per million British thermal units, traders said.
Spot prices at AECO storage hub were also stable in the C$1.37-1.42 per gigajoule area.
